subject.title: [Feature]: When building a work system with OpenClaw as the core, WebUI should remain accessible after the Gateway crashes.

question: Should OpenClaw core own a crash-survivor Control UI fallback on the Gateway port, or should this remain a documented supervisor/deployment responsibility?
rationale: The request changes Gateway availability architecture and public config/security boundaries, so the correct product contract cannot be inferred from existing code alone.

options.title: Design a core rescue sidecar
options.body: Define a supervisor-owned static fallback or rescue listener with auth/origin/TLS/device-identity semantics before implementation.

options.title: Document external supervision only
options.body: Keep core lean and point enterprise deployments to systemd/launchd/container/reverse-proxy patterns for maintenance pages and crash recovery.

options.title: Narrow to degraded-running UI
options.body: Only improve the Control UI experience while the Gateway process is alive, leaving post-crash availability out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design a core rescue sidecar
recommendation.body: Define a supervisor-owned static fallback or rescue listener with auth/origin/TLS/device-identity semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` introduced the browser Control UI and is the strongest history match for Gateway/UI product-boundary decisions.
